documents.title: Short of breath
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called: more short of breath and coughing more phlegm for a couple of weeks, scale up "a few pounds." No fever, no chest pain. Breathing at rest ok on 2 L, O2 sat on his finger meter 91-92%. Has pulmonary appt 3/3 and a heart catheter test 2/24 that pulmonary ordered.

documents.title: Pulmonary follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit 3/3/2025

Mr. Bianchi, whom we have followed for severe COPD and right heart failure since 2022, comes in with a month of more breathlessness, more productive cough, and a 4 kg weight gain. He says he has not missed his inhalers. He continues to smoke a pack a day (45 pack-years) and drinks 3-4 drinks most evenings.

Exam: JVP elevated with a prominent v wave. Low-pitched holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder with inspiration. Abdomen distended; the liver is enlarged and pulsatile. Pitting edema both legs.

Echo today: RV hypertrophy and dilation with tricuspid regurgitation.
Right heart catheterization 2/24: PA systolic pressure 35 mm Hg.

Impression: severe COPD with cor pulmonale and secondary tricuspid regurgitation.
Plan: continue tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg daily and oxygen 2 L. Stop smoking. Return 6 months.

documents.title: pulmonary
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the lung doctor monday. They said keep everything the same. I'm still up about 8 or 9 lbs. Is that ok?

documents.title: RE: pulmonary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I read their letter. Keep weighing yourself every morning and keep the salt down. If the weight keeps climbing, or the swelling reaches your knees, call and we'll see you. Let's plan a visit in May either way.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring check. Pulmonary in March: echo RV hypertrophy/dilation with TR; RHC PA systolic 35; no med changes. Weight steady since then. Breathing "like always." Cough with morning phlegm. On O2 2 L.

Exam: SpO2 92% on 2 L. Elevated JVP. Holosystolic murmur LLSB. Abdomen full. 1-2+ edema to shins.

A/P: COPD, cor pulmonale with TR, secondary polycythemia, on O2 - stable on current regimen. BMP, CBC today. Smoking: same conversation, same answer. RTC September.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.body: Yesterday's labs are fine - kidney function and potassium in range, red count about where it has been. No changes.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came for his September visit but worse this week: short of breath walking room to room, legs swollen to the knees, more cough with sputum, up at night. Taking furosemide and inhalers. On 2 L.

Exam: winded after the walk from the waiting room, settles sitting. SpO2 88% on 2 L. JVP elevated. Faint crackles at both bases, diminished throughout. Loud P2. Pitting edema to knees.

A/P
Decompensated right heart failure with probable COPD flare. Not safe to manage at home. Discussed with hospitalist - direct admission to the regional hospital medical floor today. Neighbor driving him. Med list sent with him.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 9/8/2025 (direct admission from PCP). Discharged 9/13/2025.

Presentation: worsening shortness of breath and swelling of both legs. Long-standing severe COPD with several prior admissions for exacerbations; pulmonary hypertension with chronic right heart failure; tricuspid regurgitation; secondary polycythemia; treated laryngeal and lip SCC.

Exam on admission: elevated jugular venous pressure, pitting edema of both legs, loud pulmonic component of S2, faint crackles at both bases.

Hospital course:
1. COPD exacerbation - doxycycline 100 mg twice daily x5 days and prednisone 40 mg daily x5 days, scheduled nebulizers, oxygen titrated back to his home 2 L.
2. Acute on chronic right heart failure - IV furosemide with good diuresis, transitioned back to furosemide 40 mg by mouth daily at discharge.

Discharge medications: home regimen unchanged (tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg daily, oxygen 2 L continuous); antibiotic and prednisone courses completed in hospital.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; pulmonary as scheduled. Smoking cessation advised.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call after 9/8-9/13 admission. Pt home, breathing "better than before I went in." Weight 2 kg below admission per his scale. Taking furosemide 40 daily and all inhalers, on O2 2 L. Finished the steroid and antibiotic in the hospital. No fever. Follow-up scheduled 9/23 with PCP. Reviewed red flags.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY HOSPITAL ED - PROVIDER NOTE
Seen: 11/4/2025

CC: short of breath, cough, fever.
HPI: 72-year-old man with severe COPD on 2 L home oxygen and cor pulmonale, back with several days of more dyspnea and a cough productive of yellow sputum, with fever. Was admitted in September for a COPD flare and treated with antibiotics and steroids.
Meds: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg, O2 2 L. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: current smoker 1 ppd (45 pack-years); 3-4 drinks most evenings; retired farmer.

Triage: T 38.7 C, HR 102, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air (portable tank empty on arrival).
Exam: decreased breath sounds with dullness to percussion at the right base.

Labs: leukocytosis with left shift (WBC 16.8, neutrophils 88%, bands reported).
CXR: RLL consolidation, blunted right costophrenic angle.
Thoracentesis (ED, ultrasound-guided): cloudy fluid. pH 7.10; glucose 30; LDH 600 (serum 200); protein 4.5 (serum 7.0); WBC 20,000 with 90% neutrophils; Gram stain gram-positive cocci in clusters.

Assessment: right lower lobe pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion.
ED course: blood cultures, IV vancomycin, oxygen, pulmonary and surgery consulted; chest tube placed. Admitted to medicine.

reports.text: Portable AP view after right chest tube removal. Improving right lower lobe opacity. Small residual blunting at the right base. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Improving right lower lobe consolidation and effusion; no pneumothorax after tube removal.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/4/2025 from the ED. Discharged 11/12/2025.

Diagnoses: right lower lobe pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion. Background severe COPD on home O2, cor pulmonale with tricuspid regurgitation, secondary polycythemia, treated laryngeal and lip SCC.

Course:
- Right chest tube thoracostomy 11/4 with good drainage; tube removed 11/10 with follow-up film showing improvement and no pneumothorax.
- Pleural culture: methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Vancomycin narrowed to IV cefazolin 11/7. Defervesced by day 3.
- Oxygen back to baseline 2 L. Diuretic held two days while eating poorly, then resumed at 40 mg.

Discharge medications: cephalexin 500 mg four times daily to complete 4 weeks of total antibiotic therapy (through 12/2); home regimen otherwise unchanged.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: pulmonary clinic with chest x-ray in 3-4 weeks; PCP 1-2 weeks. Strongly advised to stop smoking.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition call after 11/4-11/12 admission (pneumonia/pleural infection, chest tube). Pt taking cephalexin 4x daily, has enough through 12/2. No fever. Chest tube site with small dressing, dry. Breathing back near usual on 2 L. PCP visit booked 11/24; pulmonary 12/9.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Hyperinflated lungs. The right lower lobe consolidation has cleared and the right pleural effusion has resolved. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of right lower lobe consolidation and effusion.

documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE - FOLLOW-UP
Seen 12/9/2025 after admission for RLL pneumonia with complicated parapneumonic effusion (MSSA), treated with chest tube and antibiotics; finished cephalexin 12/2. Feels back to his usual. No fever.
Chest tube site healed.
CXR today: consolidation and effusion resolved.
Plan: continue tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol, furosemide 40 mg, O2 2 L. Smoking cessation again advised. Return in 6 months.
